notes: Site: Shopify storefront myborosil.com (www redirects 301 to non-www canonical). Tier-1 direct HTTP fetch worked throughout, no WAF/block encountered; no Playwright/Claude-in-Chrome needed. Checked: collections.json (393 total published collections, 2 pages), homepage header mega-menu, homepage 'shop by category' chip carousel (126 /collections/ links), footer (no collection links), and the site's own predictive-search endpoint (/search/suggest.json) for queries 'bestsellers','best sellers','trending','new' etc. VALID BESTSELLERS-TYPE LISTINGS FOUND: (1) /collections/bestsellers 'Best Sellers' -- the only one of these actually linked from the homepage chip grid (alt text 'Best Sellers'); confirmed real PLP via products.json. (2) /collections/larah-bestseller 'Larah Bestseller' -- for the Larah-by-Borosil sub-brand sold on the same storefront; discoverable via site search only (not in nav). (3) /collections/trending 'Trending' and (4) /collections/trending-larah 'Trending Larah' -- 'Trending Products' is an explicit target term in this brief; both discoverable via site search only (not in nav). EXCLUDED: /collections/zall 'All Best Selling' (3004 of ~3061 site-wide products, i.e. ~98% of the entire catalogue) -- not linked anywhere in header/footer/homepage chips and does NOT appear in site search results for any bestseller-related query; handle prefix 'z' and near-total-catalogue size strongly indicate this is a backend/theme utility collection (e.g. feeding a 'sort by best-selling' widget elsewhere) rather than a customer-facing Bestsellers merchandising page, so it fails criterion 2 (genuinely represents the concept) and was dropped rather than recorded. IMPORTANT CROSS-CHECK FINDING (applies to rows below, not a reason to drop them): products.json dedup-by-id shows bestsellers(2248) is a strict subset of trending(2442), and new-arrival (see na235.json, 2257) is also a strict subset of trending -- i.e. Bestsellers/New-Arrivals/Trending on the main brand nest inside each other almost completely (Bestsellers=73%, Trending=80% of the ~3061-product catalogue). On the Larah sub-brand, larah-bestseller and larah-new-arrivals (see na235.json) are BYTE-IDENTICAL product sets (1122/1122, full intersection), and trending-larah (910) is a strict subset of that same 1122-product set. This pattern (near-total catalogue coverage, strict nesting/identity across different 'concepts') is strong circumstantial evidence these may be broad automated collections rather than genuinely hand-curated bestseller/new-arrival/trending selections -- flagged per-row below for reviewer judgement rather than silently excluded or silently trusted, since each one individually does pass the open-and-confirm test (real PLP, correctly titled, reachable via nav or site search, distinct exact product count).
